title: Metric Measurement

sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of the metric system as having one 'home base' for each thing you measure. For how long or tall something is, the home base is the meter. Liters live in the 'how much liquid' house and grams live in the 'how heavy' house, so they can't be the answer for length. A centimeter is just a meter cut into 100 equal pieces.

### Question 2

Metric prefixes are like nicknames that tell you how big a number is. 'Kilo' is the nickname for a thousand, so a kilogram is just a fancy way of saying 'a thousand grams.' If you ever see kilo, picture a container holding 1,000 of the smaller unit.

### Question 3

'Milli' means you split the base unit into a thousand equal pieces and took just one piece. So a milligram is one part out of the thousand parts that make up a whole gram. That means a milligram is always a smaller amount than a gram. Careful, though: because each piece is smaller, it takes MORE of them to make the same amount, so measuring in milligrams gives you a bigger number (1 gram = 1,000 milligrams).

### Question 4

A kilogram is the big container and grams are the small units that fill it. It takes exactly 1,000 grams to fill one kilogram, so the kilogram is always the heavier, larger one.

### Question 5

When you measure the same amount with smaller units, you need more of them. One gram is worth 1,000 milligrams, so 4 grams is 4 times that, which is 4,000 milligrams. The amount of material has not changed, only the size of the unit you are counting in.

### Question 6

Going from milli to micro steps down to an even smaller unit. Each milligram is made of 1,000 micrograms, so the milligram is the larger one, and it takes 1,000 micrograms to rebuild a single milligram.

### Question 7

Some prefix mix-ups are small slips and some are huge leaps. Neighboring prefixes like centi and deci are only 10 apart, so swapping them is a small error. But a gram and a milligram are 1,000 apart, so confusing them changes the measurement by a factor of a thousand, a serious and risky mistake.

### Question 8

One liter holds 1,000 milliliters. Half a liter is half of 1,000, which is 500. So 0.5 liters equals 500 milliliters.

### Question 9

It takes 1,000 milligrams to make one gram. With only 250 of those milligrams, you have less than a whole gram, exactly one quarter of one, which is written 0.25 grams.

### Question 10

Each kilogram equals 1,000 grams. One whole kilogram is 1,000 grams, and the extra 0.2 of a kilogram adds 200 more, so 1.2 kilograms gives you 1,200 grams.

### Question 11

It takes 1,000 micrograms to make one milligram. Group 3,500 micrograms into sets of 1,000: you get 3 full sets plus half of another, which is 3.5 milligrams.

### Question 12

You cannot divide liters by milliliters directly, so first convert: 0.75 liters is 750 milliliters. Then see how many 250-milliliter portions fit into 750 milliliters, which is exactly 3.
